Two edge situations are ready to look at on the live screen.

**1. When the app can't get a link's details** — at **http://maker:4001**:
- Paste `https://unreachable.example/some-article` and press **"Get details."**
- Instead of failing silently, you'll see a clear message — *"Couldn't get this page's details. You can still add a title yourself and save"* — and the editor **still opens** so you can type your own title and save it normally. Nothing is lost just because the fetch didn't work.

**2. The very first time you open the app, with nothing saved yet** — open **http://maker:4001/?empty=1**:
- Each of the three views greets you with a friendly, purposeful message (*"Nothing here yet. Paste a link above to start,"* *"No bookmarks marked Read later yet,"* *"Nothing archived."*) rather than a blank screen. Click between the three view buttons to see each.

Do those two behave the way you'd want?

And two edge questions that are about *whether a behaviour should exist* — no screen needed, just your call:

- **Removing for good:** right now nothing is ever truly deleted — archiving tucks things away but you can always restore them. Do you want a way to **permanently delete** a bookmark, or is archive enough for this first version?
- **Saving in a hurry:** at the moment you press "Get details" before saving. Would you ever want to **save straight from a pasted link without fetching details first**, or is fetch-then-save always fine?
